input.quote: 12.4 Customer shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee during the term or for twenty-four months afterward, regardless of how the employee applies.
input.rationale: Section 12.4 imposes a one-way restriction on Customer only, covers every Vendor employee rather than personnel directly involved in the Services, runs for the term plus twenty-four months, expressly includes hiring and employment (a no-hire), and negates any general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out ("regardless of how the employee applies"). That fails every fallback element and sits in walk-away territory (no-hire plus 24-month, all-personnel scope). It also contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made "no ... no-hire commitment". We therefore take the preferred position and remove the restriction on Customer with a single conforming edit to the prohibitory operator and duration, which also resolves the internal conflict.

proposal.summary: Remove the one-way non-solicit/no-hire on Customer and confirm no such restriction applies.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We do not accept a non-solicit on Customer, and this one-way clause covering all Vendor employees for the term plus twenty-four months with no general-advertising carve-out also contradicts Section 12.3. We have replaced it with a confirmation that no such restriction applies; alternatively we could accept a mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the Services for twelve months after their involvement ends, carving out general advertisements and unsolicited approaches and without any hiring prohibition.

ops.oldText: Customer shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee during the term or for twenty-four months afterward, regardless of how the employee applies.
ops.newText: Customer is subject to no restriction on soliciting, hiring, or employing any Vendor employee.
